items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: And the bass player was named Frank Otero. Well, I learned them the instruments. And it was not long before that we used to play all these little joints on Decatur Street

ctx.x: Who was that federal player? Who was the violin player? Batiste O'Quinn. Oh yeah, I heard of him from Jack Langan. Oh, you did?

Yeah. Mama Langan used to talk about him. Batiste O'Quinn. It goes to show you what I'm telling you. It's not no line because they can verify it, you know? But then it's all the men I played. And without counting the men that I've learned myself, you know? Learned them how to play bass. Learned them how to play guitar. Like you see that little instrumentation we had, a string ensemble we had of violin, guitar, and bass. When I was playing violin, and I had a little Puerto Rican day, he played guitar. And the bass…
Did you ever have any of those old bands that, a dance band, a dance and jazz band that had an accordion in it? No.
